accessNotes: ux.mailchimp.com returns 503 / Akamai 'DNS failure' (site appears retired); the Wayback Machine was offline (503) at research time, so the original guideline text could not be read. Main secondary source: the portfolio case study of Chad Urbanick, the Mailchimp Design System designer who wrote the guideline ('Our first draft of the guidelines are live here' linking ux.mailchimp.com/patterns/data), which shows the palette work, categorical combos and example charts. Hex values below were SAMPLED from those images with ImageMagick (approximate; not published tokens). Fonts are not stated anywhere read; descriptions of type are visual observations only. A web_search summary (designsystems.one) gave Mailchimp brand yellow #ffe01b, not chart-specific.
summary: Mailchimp's product data-viz pattern (c. 2019–2020) for in-app marketing reports: quiet, warm, editorial-feeling charts with a small sans-serif title top-left, very light horizontal gridlines with abbreviated tick labels (20k, $40k), a solid dark baseline with ticks, thin 2px lines in a warm ochre, dark warm-charcoal tooltips with a vertical rule, and multi-category colour assigned from predefined accessible 'combos' that vary hue, saturation and value.

colors.categoricalNotes: Categories coloured by choosing one predefined 'Categorical Combo' and cycling through it in order (5 colours each). Sampled from the case-study image: Combo One #f97f50 coral, #4f135e plum, #99c7ef light blue, #fad173 pale yellow, #a3296e magenta; Combo Two #fad173, #99c7ef, #de4d14 burnt orange, #83249f purple, #fa8cf8 pink; Combo Four #83249f, #f97f50, #fad173, #99e0d7 mint, #4277ce blue; Combo Five #601d06 dark brown, #dd4b1d, #facf78, #99c7ef, #a22c6d; Combo Six #d99536 ochre, #99c7ef, #a3296e, #de4d14, #005733 dark green. Palette built from brand hues, each main hue expanded into eight steps along a 'predictable, mathematical curve' of hue, value and saturation.
colors.notes: All values sampled from portfolio PNGs (approximate). Single-series line charts use a warm ochre/gold (~#d99536); projections in light blue (~#99c7ef) dotted. Tooltip background warm charcoal ~#39332c with white text. Mailchimp brand yellow #ffe01b (secondary source) is not used in the chart examples. Combos designed to remain distinct under colour-vision deficiencies and to avoid placing similar colours adjacently.

typography.notes: Observed: chart titles in a regular-weight grotesque sans (looks like Mailchimp's Graphik) in near-black, noticeably larger than the small grey tick labels; the case-study headings use a serif (Mailchimp's 'Means'). Not confirmed by a published spec.

structure.gridlines: Horizontal only, very light warm grey (~#e9e9e8), 2–3 lines at round values.
structure.axisLine: Solid dark x-axis baseline (~#24201f) with short downward ticks at each date label; no y-axis line.
structure.ticks: x ticks yes (short, dark); y none.
structure.unitPlacement: In every tick label with abbreviations (20k, $40k).
structure.notes: Under the time axis, a thin segmented bar highlights periods (ochre for 'increasing' spans, light grey otherwise) with a caption whose keyword is coloured to match ('Large trends of increasing audience size').

legend.placement: top-right inline above plot for line charts; below the chart in a two-column grid for pies
legend.title: none
legend.swatchShape: short line segment (solid/dotted) for lines; small square for pie categories

marks.lines: Thin (~2px) unsmoothed lines, no markers; projection shown as dotted line in a contrasting light blue continuing from the last actual point, with a vertical dotted 'Today' rule.
marks.points: Hover point shown as a translucent enlarged circle halo in the series colour.
marks.pies: Pies used for source breakdowns (4 slices), largest slice starting at 12 o'clock clockwise, no slice borders/labels; values shown on hover tooltip ('35% • 476 Subscribers').
marks.notes: Case study lists chart types: line charts, meter charts, scatter plot, pie charts.

labels.dataLabels: None on chart; values surfaced through tooltips.
labels.numberFormat: k abbreviations (20k, $40k), $ prefix, percentages with '•' separator in tooltips.
labels.dates: Month abbreviations (Apr, Jul, Oct) with the year shown at year boundaries (2015, 2016); tooltip 'Aug 3, 2015'.

furniture.title: Short noun-phrase title top-left ('Audience Growth', 'Revenue Projection') in regular weight.
furniture.other: Captions below the chart use coloured keywords matching the encoded colour.

annotations: Vertical dotted reference rule with label at the bottom ('Today'); coloured keyword captions.
layout: Card-less, white, generous whitespace; title above plot with ~1 line gap.
interaction: Hover tooltip: dark warm-charcoal rectangle (square corners) with bold white date/category line and regular white value line, positioned above the plot and connected to the hovered point by a thin dark vertical line; hovered point gets a translucent halo.
accessibility: Colour combos pre-tested under colour-vision-deficiency simulation so adjacent categories stay distinguishable; differentiate by hue, saturation and value, not value alone.

chartTypes.notes: From the case study; original guideline text not accessible.

distinctiveRules.rule: Multi-category charts pick one predefined 5-colour 'combo' and apply its colours in sequence (e.g. coral #f97f50, plum #4f135e, light blue #99c7ef, pale yellow #fad173, magenta #a3296e).
distinctiveRules.quote: designers and engineers could simply choose a combo and our tools would simply move through the sequence of colors

distinctiveRules.rule: Categories must differ in hue, saturation AND value, never value alone.
distinctiveRules.quote: We most often used ONLY value to differentiate between categories rather than hue, saturation, AND value.

distinctiveRules.rule: Only light horizontal gridlines (2–3), y labels abbreviated with units on every tick (20k, $40k), no y-axis line.
Dark solid x baseline with short tick marks; dates as month abbreviations with year at year boundaries.
Tooltips are dark warm-charcoal boxes with white text (bold first line), tied to the point by a thin vertical rule; hovered point shows a translucent halo.
Projections continue as a dotted light-blue line after a dotted vertical 'Today' rule; legend top-right shows solid vs dotted line samples.
Chart title is a short regular-weight noun phrase top-left; no axis titles.
Pie legends sit below the pie in a two-column grid with small square swatches; values only on hover.

referenceImages.describes: Line chart 'Audience Growth': regular-weight dark sans title top-left; y labels 0/20k/40k small grey at left; two very light grey horizontal gridlines; solid near-black x baseline with short ticks, labels 2015, Apr, Jul, Oct, 2016, Apr. Single thin ochre (#d99536-ish) line, no markers. Hover state: translucent ochre halo on the point, thin black vertical line up to a dark warm-charcoal tooltip (bold white 'Aug 3, 2015', regular '$5 spent'). Below the axis a thin segmented band (ochre for growth periods, light grey otherwise) and caption 'Large trends of increasing audience size' with 'increasing' in ochre.

'Revenue Projection' line chart: title top-left, legend top-right (solid ochre line 'Revenue', dotted light-blue line 'Projected'); y labels $0/$20k/$40k left with light gridlines; dark baseline with ticks; ochre actual line then dotted light-blue projection; vertical dotted grey 'Today' rule labelled at the bottom.

Swatch sheet 'Categorical Combos' (serif heading) showing five-colour combos as stacked blocks: Combo One coral/plum/light blue/pale yellow/magenta; Combo Two pale yellow/light blue/burnt orange/purple/pink; Combo Four purple/coral/pale yellow/mint/blue; Combo Five dark brown/burnt orange/pale yellow/light blue/magenta; Combo Six ochre/light blue/magenta/burnt orange/dark green.
